chunks: For God had helped you during the Battle of Badr at a time when you were helpless. So act in compliance with the laws of God; you may well be grateful.

key_terms.أَذِلَّةٌ: Helpless, weak, or low in number/status.
key_terms.بَدْرٍ: The Battle of Badr, a pivotal early battle in Islamic history.
key_terms.فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ: So fear God / act in compliance with His laws.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Battle of Badr in relation to gratitude in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the paradox of divine victory amidst human weakness, serving as a reminder that the believers' status at Badr was not due to their own strength but God's grace. It underscores the necessity of *taqwa* (God-consciousness) and *shukr* (gratitude) as the spiritual conditions for sustaining divine favor, a theme central to the Imams' teachings on the relationship between faith and action.
